answer: Census enrollment anchors one identity per resident. An enumerator visits each household, checks a photo document, and issues one epoch-bound credential per address, a bridge between the visit and the online account. Ten fakes need ten households, ten visits and ten documents, so attacker cost rises per fake. An island of forged addresses collapses when auditors revisit a random 5% sample and revoke clusters. This is no fable of perfect coverage: movers, people without housing and corrupt enumerators are gaps, so credentials expire each epoch and enumerators certifying ghosts are slashed.
